A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ChartGalaxy and are readable throughout, including their figures, tables, equations and appendices. Retained material can be matched across the appendix reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original chart-understanding experiments, a 17-model code-generation benchmark and a user study with 16 experts evaluating 30 chart pairs.

after.justification: v4 retains those empirical results and adds dataset audits, diversity analyses, real-versus-synthetic training ablations and smaller-model evaluations.

M1.justification: The real-chart labeling procedure changes substantially. v1 describes retaining only consistent GPT-4o-mini and Gemini-2.0-Flash extractions; v4 adds GPT-4o arbitration and human correction for unresolved disagreements (Appendix B). This changes how charts receive accepted labels. The template-based synthesis and example-based generation procedures largely remain intact.

E1.justification: The real-chart source population is substantially revised: Appendix A replaces many sources, including Pinterest and Flickr, with sources such as OECD, Eurostat and the Office for National Statistics; image-search collection is also added. Some chart styles are added, and CharXiv enters the linguistic-diversity comparison. The 75 chart types, 68 layouts and three principal application tasks remain.

E2.justification: v4 Table 10 adds reported code-generation comparisons for Qwen2.5-VL-7B and Phi-4-6B; v1 only mentions excluding poorly performing models such as Phi-4. The main 17-model comparison and GPT-Image-1 user-study comparator are retained. Appendix C also adds explicit diversity comparisons with ChartQAPro and CharXiv.

E3.justification: v4 adds separate real-only and synthetic-only training conditions, Qwen2.5-VL-3B fine-tuning, and dataset-analysis protocols using geographic/topic classification, embedding distances and DreamSim/UMAP grid coverage. Section 4.1 changes the sampling description from random to balanced chart-type coverage, without establishing that existing experiments were rerun. The principal QA sample counts and benchmark metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New analyses directly examine table-extraction reliability, geographic/domain/linguistic diversity, synthetic-to-real distributional coverage, and the contribution of real versus synthetic training data (Appendices B, C and H.1). The 200-table audit and Table 8 ablations were absent from v1. Code-length, complexity, prompting and thinking-budget analyses already existed and are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same user-study confidence intervals, Wilcoxon tests and boxplots, alongside the same code-length standard deviations. v4 adds no repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests for its new model and dataset analyses.

E6.justification: Main Tables 1–4 retain their scores, but v4 adds substantial results. Table 8 reports InternVL3 chart-understanding scores of 55.74 with real data, 76.08 with synthetic data and 80.07 with both. Table 9 reports Qwen2.5-VL-3B improving from 52.42 to 71.01 on ChartGalaxy. Table 10 adds code-generation scores of 11.55 and 0.18 for Qwen2.5-VL-7B and Phi-4-6B. Appendix C adds diversity statistics and 97.62% grid coverage.

T1.justification: Appendix C newly defines coverage as the percentage of grid cells occupied by real charts that also contain synthetic charts. This adds a mathematical metric definition. The layout-optimization objective, SVG matching algorithm and existing similarity definitions are unchanged; no new theorems or proofs appear.

C1.justification: The central dataset-and-three-applications contribution remains. Its quantitative scope changes from 104,519 real and 1,151,087 synthetic charts to 61,833 and 1,701,356, and the headline variation count changes from 330 to 440. However, the per-type counts in v1 Figures 5–20 already sum to 426, versus 440 in v4, so the headline increase cannot all be treated as newly added coverage.

C2.justification: v4 newly acknowledges a North American/European geographic skew and English-only synthetic content. It interprets the new ablation gains through bounding-box-enabled instructions, extends applicability to smaller models, and argues for synthetic representativeness from grid coverage. The existing single-chart limitation and interpretations of the principal benchmark and user-study results remain.

D1.justification: v4 adds extraction-consistency criteria, the 5% numerical tolerance, arbitration/correction details, and reproducible settings for its diversity analyses. It supplies explicit source-license labels and newly specifies URL-only release of real charts. Existing training settings, API identifiers and repository links are retained. Appendix J introduces a writing-only LLM-use statement that conflicts with the documented research uses.

R1.justification: v4 adds references including InfoChartQA, OrionBench, DreamSim, LAION-5B and Foundation Models Meet Visualizations, connecting the work to multimodal chart reasoning, detection, distributional analysis and dataset release practices. The central positioning against plain-chart datasets and small infographic benchmarks is retained.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and most explanatory prose remain. v4 edits wording, adopts author-year citations, separates chart selection, templates and examples into distinct appendices, moves and expands ethics discussion, removes the NeurIPS checklist and adds an LLM-use declaration. These are editorial and organizational refinements rather than a wholesale narrative rewrite.

P2.justification: v4 revises the collection diagram, expands selected chart-gallery panels, replaces the source table's terms-of-service links with license labels, and adds Tables 8–10. It also adopts ICLR headers and adjusts sizing and placement. Most existing figures, result-table structures, example galleries and plots are retained.

improvement.justification: v4 better supports the dataset contribution through an extraction audit, real-versus-synthetic ablations and explicit diversity analyses, while improving source and processing documentation. These provide useful evidence beyond v1's aggregate performance gains. The improvement remains limited: the audit covers only exact-agreement extractions, per-condition ablation data sizes are unspecified, and Appendix J's writing-only LLM disclosure conflicts with the described methods and analyses.
